# Functional Smoke Coverage

Post-upgrade test coverage standards across Kubernetes platforms.

## Kubernetes Conformance Test Suite

The CNCF conformance program requires **100% pass rate** with zero tests skipped [13]. The conformance suite is a small subset of the total e2e test inventory:

| K8s Version | Conformance Tests | Total E2E Tests | Conformance % |
|---|---|---|---|
| v1.11 | 177 | — | — |
| v1.16 | 215 | 4,000+ | ~5% |
| v1.17 | 278 | — | — |
| v1.21 | 404 | — | — |
| v1.27 | 404 | 7,211 | 5.6% |
| v1.32 | — | — | First release with 100% conformance coverage [18] |

Sources: [12] [16] [15] [18]

API endpoint coverage grew from 11% (53 of 481 endpoints, Feb 2018) to ~94% by v1.25 [15].

## OpenShift CI Release Gating

OpenShift uses a tiered quality gate system with quantifiable thresholds [14]:

| Gate | Threshold | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| New test pass rate | 95% | For tests without Component Readiness history |
| Informing job pass rate | 70% | Minimum after one sprint |
| Blocking job flake rate | <1% | Per individual test |
| Regression detection | Statistical | Fisher's Exact test for multi-day regressions |
| Response time | 4 hours | During normal working hours |

**Maturation timeline to blocking status:** ~9 weeks minimum (1 sprint informing + 2 sprints at 70%+) [14].

**Job types:**
- Component Readiness: statistical analysis, detect regressions (e.g., 99% → 85%)
- Informing: stepping stone, removed if inactive for 2 releases
- Payload Blocking (Aggregated): multi-run parallel for statistical detection
- Payload Blocking (Single-run): up to 2 retries (3 total runs max) [14]

## Operator SDK Scorecard

6 built-in tests, binary pass/fail [17]:

| Suite | Test |
|---|---|
| Basic | basic-check-spec-test (CR spec block validation) |
| OLM | olm-bundle-validation-test |
| OLM | olm-crds-have-validation-test |
| OLM | olm-crds-have-resources-test |
| OLM | olm-spec-descriptors-test |
| OLM | olm-status-descriptors-test |

The scorecard "makes no assumptions as to the state of the operator being tested" and "does not run your operator" [17].

## Post-Upgrade Timing Expectations

| Test Type | Duration | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Smoke tests | <2 minutes | Discovery agent (Tier 3) |
| Post-flight suite | 5-15 minutes | Discovery agent (Tier 3) |
| Full conformance | 1-2 hours | Discovery agent (Tier 3) |

No industry standard exists for "what percentage of tests should run post-upgrade." All sources describe critical-path testing rather than percentage-based coverage targets.

## Counter-Perspectives

**Conformance tests are insufficient for upgrade validation:**
- Cover only "core of Kubernetes functionality" [12] — implementation-specific features are explicitly excluded
- 25%+ failure rates observed in K8s 1.5→1.7 upgrade test jobs [19]
- Deprecated APIs are the most commonly cited upgrade failure cause (multiple discovery agent sources, Tier 2-3)
- Tests are "very environment dependent" (discovery agent, Tier 2)

**Coverage percentage is the wrong metric:**
- High coverage without depth creates "false sense of security" (discovery agent, Tier 3)
- E2E tests "validate paths, not risk" (discovery agent, Tier 3)
- 100% coverage with low-quality assertions provides no bug-finding value (discovery agent, Tier 3)

**The question "what percentage is standard" may itself be flawed** — practitioners focus on critical paths and risk-based testing rather than percentage targets.

## Gaps and Limitations

- No published standard for post-upgrade functional test coverage percentage
- Conformance test counts by version are scattered across multiple sources with occasional inconsistencies (one 2026 vendor blog claims "~300" vs the v1.27 documented 404)
- OpenShift's CI thresholds are the most quantitative in the ecosystem; other platforms lack comparable published metrics
- Operator SDK scorecard validates metadata and deployability, not operational correctness [17]
